newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Geneva Opera switches home to pumping station.
newsitem.headline: Geneva Opera switches home to pumping station.

text.p: Geneva's renowned opera and ballet announced on Thursday its 1997-98 season would range from Handel's "Xerxes" to Puccini's "Madam Butterfly" -- to be staged in the city's former power generating station.

Director Renee Auphan told a news conference at the unconventional site that the year-long transfer would allow for a major rejuvenation of the company's nearby home at the 118-year-old Grand Theatre.
"We considered closing down for a year, but rejected the idea. We have to keep faith with our public, and keep our team together," the French-born former singer said.

The company's temporary home, known as the Water Power Building (Batiment des Forces Motrices) or BFM, itself went into operation in 1886 at a point where the River Rhone flows rapidly out of Lake Geneva down towards the French border.
It fell into disuse after the turn of the century, when its technology became outdated, and became a warehouse.

Geneva city authorities took it over two years ago and reshaped half the interior of the three-story grey stone construction into a theatre that can seat around 1,000 people -- some 500 less than in the Grand Theatre.

Auphan said she was convinced the acoustics would at least match those at the company's traditional base. "I have no worries that this will be a worthy home for us and for our loyal supporters," she told reporters.
The season will open in September with Offenbach's light opera "Orpheus in the Underworld" with French tenor Yann Beuron in the title role and French soprano Annick Massis singing Eurydice.
This will be followed by Mozart's "Mithridate" under the musical direction of American conductor John Keenan and starring Italian soprano Fieralla Burato and U.S. tenor Donald Kaasch.

British soprano Judith Howarth will star in a production of Donizetti's "Daughter of the Regiment" alongside U.S. tenor Paul Austin Kelly, and the BTM will also see Prokofiev's rarely-performed "Marriage in a Monastery".

The title role in "Madame Butterfly," to wrap up the season in June 1998, will be sung by Chinese soprano Sue Chen, originally from the traditional Peking opera but who later trained in Italy and has performed widely in the West and Japan.
Another Chinese-born star, mezzo-soprano Zheng Cao who has toured with the New York City Opera, will also appear as Butterfly's maid Suzuki, while American tenor Marcus Haddock will sing Pinkerton.
